The sqlglot package source is not in the head view (no sqlglot/expressions* file found), so I could not read exp.Is, exp.Null, the parser or the MySQL generator at the locked version. I did not run a round-trip such as sqlglot.parse_one('x IS NULL', read='mysql') or a generate call. I believe this is the standard shape, but that is not verified from source.

rule_sets.py:636-643 builds exp.Not(this=exp.Paren(this=exp.Is(col, Null))). sqlglot's generator emits Not as 'NOT ' + operand and Paren as '(' + inner + ')', so the MySQL text is 'NOT (x IS NULL)'. This is from reading the source and my knowledge of sqlglot; I did not run it. In MySQL with HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE, NOT binds tighter than IS, so a bare 'NOT x IS NULL' would read as '(NOT x) IS NULL'. The explicit parentheses force NOT to apply to the whole IS NULL expression, so the meaning is the intended 'x IS NOT NULL'. The code comment at 637-638 states the same reason.

rule_sets.py:637-643 emits NOT(Paren(Is(col, NULL))). The comment says that under HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE MySQL reads bare NOT x IS NULL as (NOT x) IS NULL. This matches MySQL's documented behavior: the mode gives NOT the same high precedence as '!', so it binds tighter than IS. The documented example is NOT a BETWEEN b AND c parsed as (NOT a) BETWEEN b AND c. I did not run MySQL, and the check rests on the documentation as I recall it, not on a fetched copy. The code's parenthesization is correct either way. Absolute-claim input: with the mode on, NOT x IS NULL is read as (NOT x) IS NULL, so the comment's reading holds.
